comparisons.peer_topic: Capital Metrics: TCE, RoTCE, and TBVPS
comparisons.peer_summary: Tangible common equity (TCE), return on tangible common equity (RoTCE), and tangible book value per share (TBVPS) are used by management and investors to assess equity usage and capital strength, providing alternative measures of performance and tangible asset levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C disclose specific forward-looking capital metrics (ROE, ROTE, or RoTCE) and the associated risk that targets or expectations may not be achieved. GS explicitly states that its targets for ROE and ROTE are subject to risk due to changes in business mix and strategy execution. Citi similarly highlights Tangible Common Equity (TCE) and Return on Tangible Common Equity (RoTCE) as key metrics used to assess capital strength, aligning with GS's focus on tangible equity returns, though Citi's excerpt focuses more on the definition/utility of the metric rather than the explicit risk of missing a target in the provided sentence.

sentences.text: Statements about our target ROE, ROTE, efficiency ratio and expense savings, and how they can be achieved, are based on our current expectations regarding our business prospects and are subject to the risk that we may be unable to achieve our targets due to, among other things, changes in our business mix and inability to grow our businesses and execute our strategy.
For more information on TCE, RoTCE and TBVPS, see "Capital Resources-Tangible Common Equity, Book Value Per Share, Tangible Book Value Per Share and Return on Equity" below.
Citi believes TCE and RoTCE are useful to investors, industry analysts and others by providing alternative measures of capital strength and performance.
